    11	
    12	/-!
    13	# Local generators of a finite projective module (DAT-A generators corollary)
    14	
    15	Worksheet §2.2.3a (`informal/spec-dat-a.md` §4): for a finite projective module `Q`
    16	over `B` — the engine's `H⁰` on the fibrewise-vanishing locus (`datumRigidEngine`) —
    17	and a prime `p` where the fibre `Q ⊗ κ(p)` is nontrivial, there is a basic open
    18	`D(f) ∋ p` and a GLOBAL element `q : Q` whose image in `Q ⊗ κ(q')` is nonzero for
    19	EVERY `q' ∈ D(f)`:
    20	
    21	> Zariski-locally on `Spec B`, a fibrewise-nonzero section exists.
    22	
    23	Route: finite + projective ⟹ finitely presented + flat; `Module.freeLocus_eq_univ`
    24	gives freeness at `p`; `Module.FinitePresentation.exists_free_localizedModule_powers`
    25	localizes the freeness to a basic open `D(f)`; a basis element of the localized module
    26	has numerator `q`; at every `q' ∈ D(f)` the coordinate functional of the basis,
    27	composed with the away-lift `B_f →+* κ(q')` (legal since `f ∉ q'` makes `f` invertible
    28	in the residue field), evaluates the fibre image of `q` to a nonzero power of the image
    29	of `f` — no localized tensor products are formed.
    30	
    31	Consumers (stated for verbatim consumption): DAT-B's coverage (a local divisor
    32	presentation of an arbitrary functor point through DAT-A's `sectionLocalEquations`) and
    33	DD-R's local generators (dat-d-worksheet §3.4). The `Nontrivial` fibre input is the
    34	rank clause consumers hold through FLV/DAT-3.
    35	-/
    36	
    37	set_option autoImplicit false
    38	
    39	universe u
    40	
    41	open scoped TensorProduct
    42	
    43	namespace Module
    44	
    45	variable {B : Type u} [CommRing B] {Q : Type u} [AddCommGroup Q] [Module B Q]
    46	
    47	/-- If some localization of `Q` away from an element of `p.primeCompl` is trivial, the
    48	residue-field fibre at `p` is trivial: the annihilating power of `f` is invertible in
    49	`κ(p)`. -/
    50	private lemma subsingleton_tensor_residueField_of_subsingleton_away
    51	    (p : PrimeSpectrum B) (f : B) (hf : f ∉ p.asIdeal)
    52	    (hsub : Subsingleton (LocalizedModule.Away f Q)) :
    53	    Subsingleton (Q ⊗[B] p.asIdeal.ResidueField) := by
    54	  have hx : algebraMap B p.asIdeal.ResidueField f ≠ 0 := fun h0 =>
    55	    hf (Ideal.algebraMap_residueField_eq_zero.mp h0)
    56	  refine subsingleton_of_forall_eq 0 (fun z => ?_)
    57	  induction z using TensorProduct.induction_on with
    58	  | zero => rfl
    59	  | add u v hu hv => rw [hu, hv, add_zero]
    60	  | tmul q c =>
    61	      -- the localized image of `q` vanishes, so a power of `f` kills `q`
    62	      have hmk : (LocalizedModule.mk q 1 : LocalizedModule.Away f Q)
    63	          = LocalizedModule.mk 0 1 := Subsingleton.elim _ _
    64	      obtain ⟨u, hu⟩ := LocalizedModule.mk_eq.mp hmk
    65	      rw [one_smul, one_smul, smul_zero] at hu
    66	      -- transfer `u • q = 0` through the tensor, inverting `u` in the residue field
    67	      have hu_ne : algebraMap B p.asIdeal.ResidueField (u : B) ≠ 0 := by
    68	        obtain ⟨n, hn⟩ := u.2
    69	        intro h0
    70	        rw [← hn, map_pow] at h0
    71	        exact hx (pow_eq_zero_iff' .. |>.mp h0).1
    72	      have hu' : (u : B) • q = 0 := hu
    73	      have hkill : q ⊗ₜ[B] ((algebraMap B p.asIdeal.ResidueField (u : B))
    74	          * ((algebraMap B p.asIdeal.ResidueField (u : B))⁻¹ * c)) = 0 := by
    75	        have hz : ((u : B) • q) ⊗ₜ[B]
    76	            ((algebraMap B p.asIdeal.ResidueField (u : B))⁻¹ * c) = 0 := by
    77	          rw [hu', TensorProduct.zero_tmul]
    78	        rw [TensorProduct.smul_tmul, Algebra.smul_def] at hz
    79	        exact hz
    80	      rwa [mul_inv_cancel_left₀ hu_ne] at hkill
    81	
    82	/-- **The generators corollary** (worksheet §2.2.3a; DAT-B/DD-R's local generators):
    83	for a finite projective `B`-module `Q` with nontrivial residue-field fibre at `p`,
    84	there are `f ∉ p` and a global `q : Q` whose image in `Q ⊗ κ(q')` is nonzero for
    85	**every** prime `q'` of the basic open `D(f)` — Zariski-locally, a fibrewise-nonzero
    86	section of `Q` exists. -/
    87	theorem exists_fibrewise_tmul_ne_zero_of_projective
    88	    [Module.Finite B Q] [Module.Projective B Q] (p : PrimeSpectrum B)
    89	    (hp : Nontrivial (Q ⊗[B] p.asIdeal.ResidueField)) :
    90	    ∃ f : B, f ∉ p.asIdeal ∧ ∃ q : Q, ∀ q' : PrimeSpectrum B, f ∉ q'.asIdeal →
    91	      (q ⊗ₜ (1 : q'.asIdeal.ResidueField) : Q ⊗[B] q'.asIdeal.ResidueField) ≠ 0 := by
    92	  classical
    93	  haveI : Module.FinitePresentation B Q := Module.finitePresentation_of_projective B Q
    94	  -- freeness at `p`, localized to a basic open `D(f)`
    95	  haveI hfree_p : Module.Free (Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal)
    96	      (LocalizedModule.AtPrime p.asIdeal Q) := by
    97	    have hmem : p ∈ Module.freeLocus B Q := by
    98	      rw [Module.freeLocus_eq_univ]
    99	      trivial
   100	    exact Module.mem_freeLocus.mp hmem
   101	  obtain ⟨f, hf, hfree, -⟩ :=
   102	    Module.FinitePresentation.exists_free_localizedModule_powers p.asIdeal.primeCompl
   103	      (LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap p.asIdeal.primeCompl Q)
   104	      (Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal)
   105	  haveI := hfree
   106	  -- the localized module is nontrivial (else the fibre at `p` would be trivial)
   107	  haveI hnt : Nontrivial (LocalizedModule.Away f Q) := by
   108	    by_contra hns
   109	    rw [not_nontrivial_iff_subsingleton] at hns
   110	    exact (not_subsingleton _)
   111	      (subsingleton_tensor_residueField_of_subsingleton_away p f hf hns)
   112	  -- a basis element, with numerator `q` and denominator a power of `f`
   113	  let b := Module.Free.chooseBasis (Localization (.powers f)) (LocalizedModule.Away f Q)
   114	  obtain ⟨i₀⟩ := b.index_nonempty
   115	  obtain ⟨⟨q, s⟩, hqs⟩ : ∃ ms : Q × (Submonoid.powers f),
   116	      (LocalizedModule.mk ms.1 ms.2 : LocalizedModule.Away f Q) = b i₀ :=
   117	    LocalizedModule.induction_on (fun m s => ⟨(m, s), rfl⟩) (b i₀)
   118	  refine ⟨f, hf, q, fun q' hq' => ?_⟩
   119	  -- the residue field of `q'` receives the away-localization
   120	  have hx : algebraMap B q'.asIdeal.ResidueField f ≠ 0 := fun h0 =>
   121	    hq' (Ideal.algebraMap_residueField_eq_zero.mp h0)
   122	  have hxu : IsUnit (algebraMap B q'.asIdeal.ResidueField f) :=
   123	    isUnit_iff_ne_zero.mpr hx
   124	  set g' : Localization (Submonoid.powers f) →+* q'.asIdeal.ResidueField :=
   125	    IsLocalization.Away.lift f hxu with hg'
   126	  -- the evaluation functional: coordinate of the basis at `i₀`, pushed to `κ(q')`
   127	  set Λ : Q ⊗[B] q'.asIdeal.ResidueField →ₗ[B] q'.asIdeal.ResidueField :=
   128	    TensorProduct.lift (LinearMap.mk₂ B
   129	      (fun m c => g' ((b.coord i₀) (LocalizedModule.mk m 1)) * c)
   130	      (fun m m' c => by
   131	        rw [show (LocalizedModule.mk (m + m') 1 : LocalizedModule.Away f Q)
   132	            = LocalizedModule.mk m 1 + LocalizedModule.mk m' 1 from
   133	          (LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap (.powers f) Q).map_add m m', map_add, map_add,
   134	          add_mul])
   135	      (fun a m c => by
   136	        rw [show (LocalizedModule.mk (a • m) 1 : LocalizedModule.Away f Q)
   137	            = a • LocalizedModule.mk m 1 from
   138	          (LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap (.powers f) Q).map_smul a m,
   139	          ← algebraMap_smul (Localization (Submonoid.powers f)) a, map_smul,
   140	          smul_eq_mul, map_mul, IsLocalization.Away.lift_eq, ← Algebra.smul_def,
   141	          smul_mul_assoc])
   142	      (fun m c c' => by rw [mul_add])
   143	      (fun a m c => by rw [mul_smul_comm])) with hΛ
   144	  -- `Λ` evaluates the fibre image of `q` to a nonzero power of the image of `f`
   145	  intro h0
   146	  have hval := congrArg Λ h0
   147	  rw [map_zero, hΛ, TensorProduct.lift.tmul] at hval
   148	  -- compute the coordinate: `mk q 1 = s • b i₀`, and `coord i₀ (b i₀) = 1`
   149	  have hmk1 : (LocalizedModule.mk q 1 : LocalizedModule.Away f Q) = (s : B) • b i₀ := by
   150	    rw [← hqs]
   151	    change _ = (s : B) • (LocalizedModule.mk q s : LocalizedModule.Away f Q)
   152	    rw [LocalizedModule.smul'_mk, ← Submonoid.smul_def, LocalizedModule.mk_cancel]
   153	  have hcoord : (b.coord i₀) (LocalizedModule.mk q 1)
   154	      = algebraMap B (Localization (Submonoid.powers f)) (s : B) := by
   155	    rw [hmk1, ← algebraMap_smul (Localization (Submonoid.powers f)) (s : B) (b i₀),
   156	      map_smul, smul_eq_mul, Basis.coord_apply, Basis.repr_self,
   157	      Finsupp.single_eq_same, mul_one]
   158	  rw [LinearMap.mk₂_apply, hcoord, IsLocalization.Away.lift_eq, mul_one] at hval
   159	  -- the value is a nonzero power of the image of `f`
   160	  obtain ⟨n, hn⟩ := s.2
   161	  rw [← hn, map_pow] at hval
   162	  exact pow_ne_zero n hx hval
   163	
   164	end Module

AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/Pic0RankOnePresentation.lean:708:Together with `exists_baseOpen_evaluation_generator`, this is the immediate local divisor

280	
   281	* if a set of elements meets the complement of every prime, it generates the unit ideal
   282	  (otherwise it sits inside a maximal ideal);
   283	* the unit ideal is spanned by a **finite** subset (`Ideal.span_eq_top_iff_finite`), which is
   284	  the compactness of `Spec A` in the form the sheaf property wants.
   285	
   286	The localizations are then the canonical `Localization.Away f`, so no family of test algebras
   287	has to be threaded through the statement either. -/
   288	
   289	section Pointwise
   290	
   291	/-- An indexed family of ring elements whose basic opens cover `Spec A` generates the unit ideal.
   292	
   293	**This is mathlib's `PrimeSpectrum.iSup_basicOpen_eq_top_iff` in another spelling**, and it is
   294	written through it rather than re-proved — the audit finding `I-1659`.  An earlier version proved
   295	it directly (a set in no prime is in no maximal ideal) because plain `exact?` fails on this goal;
   296	`exact?` failing is not absence, and the mathlib lemma is stated as an `iSup` of basic opens over
   297	an *indexed family*, which is exactly the shape the use site below has.
   298	
   299	Kept as a named lemma only because the `Set.range`/`iSup` translation is two tactic lines that
   300	would otherwise be inlined twice. -/
   301	theorem span_eq_top_of_forall_prime {A : Type u} [CommRing A] {ι : Type*} (f : ι → A)
   302	    (h : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum A, ∃ i, f i ∉ p.asIdeal) :
   303	    Ideal.span (Set.range f) = ⊤ := by
   304	  rw [← PrimeSpectrum.iSup_basicOpen_eq_top_iff]
   305	  ext p
   306	  simpa using h p
   307	
   308	variable {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
   309	
   310	/-- **THE POINTWISE REDUCTION**: if every prime of `A` has *some* basic open neighbourhood on
   311	which the plus construction is trivial, it is trivial at `A`.
   312	
   313	No covering family in the statement: the witnesses are chosen at the primes, shown to span,
   314	cut down to a finite subfamily by `Ideal.span_eq_top_iff_finite`, and fed to
   315	`PicEtAff.subsingleton_of_away`.  The hypothesis is about `Localization.Away f`, a BASIC OPEN and
   316	NOT a local ring (`IsLocalRing (Localization.Away f)` does not hold); a lane holding a genuinely
   317	local computation has `Localization.AtPrime p`, and the `AtPrime`-to-`Away` bridge is spreading
   318	out and is unbuilt.  So this is the interface for a computation over basic opens, which is a
   319	weaker thing than the header of this file originally claimed. -/
   320	theorem PicEtAff.subsingleton_of_forall_prime
   321	    (h : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum A, ∃ f : A, f ∉ p.asIdeal ∧
   322	      Subsingleton (PicEtAff C (Localization.Away f))) :
   323	    Subsingleton (PicEtAff C A) := by
   324	  classical
   325	  choose f hf hsub using h
   326	  have hspan : Ideal.span (Set.range f) = ⊤ :=
   327	    span_eq_top_of_forall_prime f fun p => ⟨p, hf p⟩
   328	  obtain ⟨t, hts, ht⟩ := (Ideal.span_eq_top_iff_finite (Set.range f)).mp hspan
   329	  refine PicEtAff.subsingleton_of_away C (ι := {x // x ∈ t}) (fun i => i.1)

    11	
    12	`DivSchemeCertZarSeed.lean` reduced the DD-R certificate gate to *away-local* certificates
    13	over a span-`⊤` family.  The geometry that produces such certificates, however, is
    14	pointwise on the base: the support tube (`Scheme.LocalEquations.exists_supportTube`)
    15	isolates the pieces over a Zariski neighbourhood **of one base point at a time**, and the
    16	fibre analyses all read at a single `p : PrimeSpectrum R`.

    18	This file closes that gap with the quasi-compactness step.  If for every prime `p` there
    19	is some `r ∉ p` over whose away localization the system is certified, then the good
    20	elements span the unit ideal (their basic opens cover `Spec R`), so finitely many of them
    21	already do — and `isLocallyCertified_of_forall_exists_away` applies.

    24	one base point at a time, exactly the shape the landed fibre machinery delivers.

    52	/-- **Pointwise good elements span the unit ideal, finitely.** If a predicate `P` on `R`

    70	    show (1 : R) ∈ Ideal.span {r : R | P r}

    76	    constructor
    77	    · rintro ⟨i, rfl⟩
    78	      exact (T.equivFin.symm i).2
    79	    · intro hx
    80	      exact ⟨T.equivFin ⟨x, hx⟩, by simp⟩

    96	/-- Two unit Čech cocycles on a pointed cover are cohomologous if a `0`-cochain of unit
    97	sections conjugates their pair values into each other. -/
    98	lemma unitsCocycle_isCohomologous {𝒰 : X.PointedCover} {γ δ : X.unitsCocycle 𝒰}
    99	    (α : ∀ i, Γ(X, 𝒰.opens i)ˣ)
   100	    (h : ∀ i j, X.unitsRestrict inf_le_left (α i) * unitsEvInf γ i j
   101	      = unitsEvInf δ i j * X.unitsRestrict inf_le_right (α j)) :
   102	    γ.IsCohomologous δ :=
   103	  (OneCocycle.isCohomologous_iff_evInf γ δ).mpr ⟨α, h⟩

   105	/-! ## Local equations -/
   106	
   107	/-- Local equations for an effective Cartier divisor on `X`, adapted to a pointed cover:
   108	a section `eqn x` on each member `cover.opens x`, whose germ at every point of that member
   109	is a nonzerodivisor (`regular`) and whose overlap ratios `eqn x / eqn y` are units
   110	(`ratio_isUnit`). The class of the associated Čech cocycle of transition units is the
   111	divisor class `𝒪(D)`, see `LocalEquations.picClass`. -/
   112	structure LocalEquations (X : Scheme.{u}) : Type u where
   113	  /-- The pointed cover on whose members the local equations live. -/
   114	  cover : X.PointedCover
   115	  /-- The local equation on the member `cover.opens x`. -/
   116	  eqn : ∀ x, Γ(X, cover.opens x)
   117	  /-- Each local equation is regular: its germ at every point of its member is a
   118	  nonzerodivisor in the stalk. This is the primitive form of regularity; it implies the
   119	  regularity of every restriction (`eqn_restrict_mem_nonZeroDivisors`). -/
   120	  regular : ∀ (x y : X) (hy : y ∈ cover.opens x),
   121	    (X.presheaf.germ (cover.opens x) y hy).hom (eqn x) ∈ nonZeroDivisors (X.presheaf.stalk y)
   122	  /-- On the overlap `cover.opens x ⊓ cover.opens y` the two equations differ by a unit
   123	  factor `eqn x = u · eqn y`, so that `𝒪(D)` is invertible. -/
   124	  ratio_isUnit : ∀ x y, ∃ u : Γ(X, cover.opens x ⊓ cover.opens y)ˣ,
   125	    (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE inf_le_left).op).hom (eqn x)
   126	      = (u : Γ(X, cover.opens x ⊓ cover.opens y))
   127	        * (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE inf_le_right).op).hom (eqn y)
   128	
   129	namespace LocalEquations
   130	
   131	variable (d : X.LocalEquations)
   132	
   133	/-- Section-level regularity: the restriction of `eqn x` to any sub-open `W ≤ cover.opens x`
   134	is a nonzerodivisor in `Γ(X, W)`. Sections of a sheaf inject into the product of their
   135	germs, so nonzerodivisibility of the germs (the field `regular`) propagates to every
   136	restriction. -/
   137	lemma eqn_restrict_mem_nonZeroDivisors (x : X) {W : X.Opens} (hW : W ≤ d.cover.opens x) :
   138	    (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE hW).op).hom (d.eqn x) ∈ nonZeroDivisors Γ(X, W) := by
   139	  rw [mem_nonZeroDivisors_iff_right]
   140	  intro t ht
   141	  apply TopCat.Presheaf.section_ext X.sheaf W t 0
   142	  intro y hy
   143	  rw [map_zero]
   144	  have key : (X.presheaf.germ W y hy).hom t
   145	      * (X.presheaf.germ W y hy).hom ((X.presheaf.map (homOfLE hW).op).hom (d.eqn x)) = 0 := by
   146	    rw [← map_mul, ht, map_zero]
   147	  rw [TopCat.Presheaf.germ_res_apply] at key
   148	  exact (mul_left_mem_nonZeroDivisors_eq_zero_iff (d.regular x y (hW hy))).mp
   149	    (by rw [mul_comm] at key; exact key)

   151	/-! ## The transition units -/
   152	
   153	/-- The transition unit `g x y = eqn x / eqn y ∈ Γ(X, 𝒰x ⊓ 𝒰y)ˣ`: the unique unit with
   154	`eqn x|∩ = g x y · eqn y|∩`. -/
   155	noncomputable def ratioUnit (x y : X) : Γ(X, d.cover.opens x ⊓ d.cover.opens y)ˣ :=
   156	  (d.ratio_isUnit x y).choose
   157	
   158	/-- The defining property of the transition unit `g x y`: on the overlap,
   159	`eqn x = g x y · eqn y`. -/
   160	lemma eqn_restrict_eq (x y : X) :
   161	    (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE inf_le_left).op).hom (d.eqn x)
   162	      = (d.ratioUnit x y : Γ(X, d.cover.opens x ⊓ d.cover.opens y))
   163	        * (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE inf_le_right).op).hom (d.eqn y) :=
   164	  (d.ratio_isUnit x y).choose_spec
   165	
   166	/-- Uniqueness of the transition unit: any unit `u` with `eqn x = u · eqn y` on the
   167	overlap equals `g x y`. Regularity of `eqn y` (its restriction is a nonzerodivisor) makes
   168	the ratio unique. -/
   169	lemma ratioUnit_unique (x y : X) (u : Γ(X, d.cover.opens x ⊓ d.cover.opens y)ˣ)
   170	    (hu : (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE inf_le_left).op).hom (d.eqn x)
   171	      = (u : Γ(X, d.cover.opens x ⊓ d.cover.opens y))
   172	        * (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE inf_le_right).op).hom (d.eqn y)) :
   173	    u = d.ratioUnit x y := by
   174	  refine Units.ext ?_
   175	  refine (mul_cancel_right_mem_nonZeroDivisors
   176	    (d.eqn_restrict_mem_nonZeroDivisors y (inf_le_right : d.cover.opens x ⊓ d.cover.opens y
   177	      ≤ d.cover.opens y))).mp ?_
   178	  rw [← hu, d.eqn_restrict_eq x y]

   181	`𝒰x ⊓ 𝒰y ⊓ 𝒰z`: `g x y · g y z = g x z`. Proved by multiplying through by the regular
   182	`eqn z` and cancelling. Mirrors `Scheme.unitsEvInf_trans`. -/
   183	lemma ratioUnit_trans (x y z : X) :
   184	    X.unitsRestrict (inf_le_left :
   185	          d.cover.opens x ⊓ d.cover.opens y ⊓ d.cover.opens z
   186	            ≤ d.cover.opens x ⊓ d.cover.opens y)
   187	        (d.ratioUnit x y)
   188	      * X.unitsRestrict (inf_le_inf_right _ inf_le_right :
   189	          d.cover.opens x ⊓ d.cover.opens y ⊓ d.cover.opens z
   190	            ≤ d.cover.opens y ⊓ d.cover.opens z)
   191	          (d.ratioUnit y z)
   192	      = X.unitsRestrict (inf_le_inf_right _ inf_le_left :
   193	          d.cover.opens x ⊓ d.cover.opens y ⊓ d.cover.opens z
   194	            ≤ d.cover.opens x ⊓ d.cover.opens z)
   195	          (d.ratioUnit x z) := by
   196	  refine Units.ext ?_
   197	  -- work at the level of underlying sections on the triple overlap
   198	  rw [Units.val_mul, coe_unitsRestrict, coe_unitsRestrict, coe_unitsRestrict]
   199	  -- cancel the regular restriction of `eqn z`
   200	  refine (mul_cancel_right_mem_nonZeroDivisors
   201	    (d.eqn_restrict_mem_nonZeroDivisors z (inf_le_right :
   202	      d.cover.opens x ⊓ d.cover.opens y ⊓ d.cover.opens z ≤ d.cover.opens z))).mp ?_
   203	  -- `g x z · eqn z = eqn x` on the triple overlap
   204	  have hA := congrArg (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE (inf_le_inf_right _ inf_le_left :
   205	      d.cover.opens x ⊓ d.cover.opens y ⊓ d.cover.opens z
   206	        ≤ d.cover.opens x ⊓ d.cover.opens z)).op).hom (d.eqn_restrict_eq x z)

    (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam)

    (f : P.cover.Carrier)
    (y : Sheaf.HModule P.datum.sheaf 0)

      ∃ (y : Sheaf.HModule P.datum.sheaf 0)

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0RankOneLocusNative

/-!
# The canonical native rank-one presentation contract

`PicRankOneLocalPresentation` deliberately leaves the geometric producer fields explicit.
This file fixes the module part of that contract: for a tied cocycle datum `D`, the module is
always `D.nativeModule` and its base-ring comparison is always
`D.nativeModuleKSheafIso`.  The native piece trivializations supply the line-bundle field;
arbitrary-cartesian pushforward base change and the cohomology/rank certificates stay as
explicit obligations.

The resulting contract is therefore an adapter interface for a future producer, rather than a
second choice of a line bundle.  Its conversion is consumed directly by the public
`PicRankOneOpen` membership theorem below; no unrelated module or untied class can enter
through this bridge, and the adapter itself does not provide the geometric certificates.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3

universe u

open CategoryTheory Limits TopologicalSpace Opposite MonoidalCategory
  CartesianMonoidalCategory

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
attribute [local instance 10000] relCurve.instOver

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
variable {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
variable (pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsFinite pi]

/-! ## The native adapter contract -/

/--
A lambda-tied rank-one presentation whose module is canonically the native module of its
cocycle datum.

The fields after `datum_class` are exactly the remaining producer obligations.  The line-bundle
certificate is derived from the canonical piece trivializations, so a field-level H⁰/H¹
calculation or an unrelated line bundle cannot be silently substituted for the native
evaluation module.
-/
structure PicRankOneNativePresentation
    (lam : picDegLayer C (genus C : ℤ) (overSpec k A)) : Type (u + 1) where
  cover : Algebra.EtaleCover A
  representative : descentClasses C cover
  represents :
    PicEtAff.mk C cover representative = picEtAffineEquiv C A lam.1
  datum : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C cover.Carrier pi
  datum_class :
    (representative : relPic C (overSpec k cover.Carrier)) =
      relPicMk C (overSpec k cover.Carrier) datum.cechPicClass
  native_pushforward_base_change :
    ∀ {T' X' : Scheme.{u}}
      (g : T' ⟶ Spec (.of cover.Carrier)) (f' : X' ⟶ T')
      (g' : X' ⟶ relCurve C cover.Carrier)
      (sq : IsPullback g' f'
        (relCurve C cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of cover.Carrier)) g),
      IsIso ((canonicalBaseChangeMap sq).app datum.nativeModule)
  h1_vanishing : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule datum.sheaf 1)
  h0_finite : Module.Finite cover.Carrier (Sheaf.HModule datum.sheaf 0)
  h0_projective : Module.Projective cover.Carrier (Sheaf.HModule datum.sheaf 0)
  h0_rank_one :
    ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum cover.Carrier,
      Module.rankAtStalk (Sheaf.HModule datum.sheaf 0) p = 1

namespace PicRankOneNativePresentation

variable {pi} {lam : picDegLayer C (genus C : ℤ) (overSpec k A)}

/-- Convert the native adapter contract to the existing local-presentation contract.

The two native bridge fields are inserted definitionally; all other fields are transported
without weakening or adding hypotheses.
-/
noncomputable def toLocalPresentation
    (P : PicRankOneNativePresentation pi lam) :
    PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam :=
  { cover := P.cover
    representative := P.representative
    represents := P.represents
    datum := P.datum
    datum_class := P.datum_class
    module := P.datum.nativeModule
    module_iso := P.datum.nativeModuleKSheafIso
    line_bundle := P.datum.nativeModule_isLineBundle
    native_pushforward_base_change := P.native_pushforward_base_change
    h1_vanishing := P.h1_vanishing
    h0_finite := P.h0_finite
    h0_projective := P.h0_projective
    h0_rank_one := P.h0_rank_one }

theorem nonempty_localPresentation
    (P : PicRankOneNativePresentation pi lam) :
    Nonempty (PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam) :=
  ⟨P.toLocalPresentation⟩

end PicRankOneNativePresentation

/-! ## Immediate rank-one-locus consumer -/

/--
An arbitrary-affine family of native contracts supplies the existing public rank-one-locus
consumer.  The family is quantified in exactly the same way as
`PicRankOneOpen.LocalPresentationCondition`; the conversion only canonicalizes the module
choice and does not manufacture any of the remaining geometric certificates.
-/
theorem mem_picRankOneOpen_of_nativePresentations
    {T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
    {lam : (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).obj T}
    (h : ∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
        (t : overSpec k A ⟶ T.unop),
        Nonempty (PicRankOneNativePresentation pi
          ((picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).map t.op lam))) :
    lam ∈ (PicRankOneOpen pi).obj T := by
  apply mem_picRankOneOpen_of_localPresentations pi
  intro A _ _ t
  obtain ⟨P⟩ := h A t
  exact P.nonempty_localPresentation

end AlgebraicGeometry

name: horizon
description: How to work inside an Archon Horizon workspace — orient from on-disk state, pick the highest-value formalization work, record progress as commits, and coordinate. Load this first; it points to the specialized skills for detail. Editable per workspace.
---

You are working inside an **Archon Horizon** workspace: a place where AI agents
formalize mathematics in Lean 4 across one or more projects. This skill is the
map. It is deliberately short and **you can edit it** (it lives at
`.claude/skills/horizon/SKILL.md` in this workspace) — tune it to how you want to
work. It points to focused skills; load those on demand rather than up front.

## You are a team; the workspace is where teams collaborate

Think of your session as **one team**: you (the lead) plus the subagents you
spawn as your **workers**, with the tools and skills available to you. A
`horizon run` is your team working through its task. Other runs are **other
teams** working in parallel on the *same shared workspace* — one Lean project set,
one roadmap/board, one ledger, one inbox.

You do not manage other teams and they do not manage you. You coordinate through
**shared state**, not meetings:

- **The board (roadmap)** is the shared plan. Keep your items' status/owner/
  milestone current so other teams see what you hold and where it's going.
- **The inbox** is asynchronous messaging + memory across teams (skill:
  `horizon-inbox`): shared notes, per-task private items, and direct messages to
  another team.
- **Commits** are the durable record; reading recent ledger history tells you what
  other teams just produced (skill: `project-git`).

Before you start, be aware of who else is live (see "Is another run live" below).
A short **synchronizer** digest is printed to stderr at the start of your CLI
commands. Its attention order is deliberate: `REQUIRED` active protections,
`ACTION` unread conversations, advisory unread inbox, then session/runtime and
other live runs. Read it; it is how you stay aware without asking anyone. A new
conversation or reply invalidates the digest cache immediately. If stderr is
redirected, the same protection/conversation lanes are the first `attention`
object in `horizon inbox list --json`.

## Orient (pull state, don't assume it)

**Start here:** your prompt says nothing about who ran before you. Usually
somebody did — often minutes ago, often on this same task, and their report was
written for you. Skill: `horizon-start` — one cheap pass that works out which
situation you were launched into (fresh run, hand-off from the session that just
finished, resume after a crash, or outside a run) and what to read for each.

The workspace root is `$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT`; your shell may start in a member
project rather than at that root. The absolute path to this skill is
`$ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL`. Live state is under
`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/.archon-horizon/` and the manifest is
`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/config.yaml`. Read what you need, when you need it — via the
`horizon` CLI (invoke it as `"$HORIZON_BIN" …`):

- **Roadmap** — YOUR strategy sketch across *all* projects, kept as a nested
  outline. `"$HORIZON_BIN" roadmap list` renders the indented tree with per-parent
  progress (`active · 3/7 done`); `--focus <id>` shows one subtree, `--max-depth 0`
  the top level only. Structure it: nest sub-goals with `--parent`, keep your
  item's status/strategy current as you work. It doubles as the **project board**:
  set `--owner <team>` (who holds it), `--milestone <label>` (a free grouping tag,
  filter with `roadmap list --milestone <label>`), and pin concrete deliverables
  with `--pin-commit <sha>`. Roadmap commands print a **warning**
  when parent/child statuses disagree (all sub-items done but parent open, or a
  done parent with open children) — nothing is auto-corrected; you decide whether
  to fix it or leave it (it may be intentional). They also warn when too many
  milestones claim simultaneous `active` focus.
- **Tasks** — a specific piece of work, usually the one a human launched and is
  watching. `"$HORIZON_BIN" task …`. Task commands warn when the open queue grows
  beyond the advisory limit or a `running` status looks orphaned.
- **Inbox** — how teams talk across sessions and projects. Leave a note for the
  next session; read what past ones left. `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox …` (skill:
  `horizon-inbox`). Items can be **owned by your task** (private, e.g. your team's
  memory) or **shared with everyone** (the default); read-state is per-team, so
  `inbox list --mine --unread` is your team's fresh queue, and you can
  direct-message another team with `--to task:<id>`. Inbox commands warn when the
  open working set—especially `memory` and `info`—needs review.
- **Inbox attention order** — before edits, inspect all open `protection` items
  (standing constraints, whether read or unread), then open unread
  `conversation` items and reply or mark them read. Other kinds are advisory
  context. In an agent session an unqualified `inbox list` defaults to open items
  and sorts in this order; use an explicit status to audit history.
- **Conversation discipline** — use a conversation only when a reply/decision is
  expected. Search and reuse an open thread before starting one. Its initiator is
  a participant and owns closure: after consuming the answer, add a concise
  conclusion if needed and archive the thread. Reply to human-started threads but
  leave their closure to the human unless asked otherwise (skill: `horizon-inbox`).
- **Blueprint graph** — declaration dependencies and what's proved. `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> …` (skill: `hgraph`).
  Each node is also an **hgraph** file with attached comments/reviews —
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` ranks what to prove next, and node-scoped failure memory
  goes on the node itself (skill: `hgraph`).
- **Memory** — durable facts/dead-ends live in the inbox: read with
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox list --kind memory --json`, write with
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox add --kind memory --to horizon --body …`.
- **Usage** — your token/cost consumption this session and run, budget headroom,
  and recent rate-limit signals: `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json`. See
  "Pace yourself" below for how to act on it.

## Your session's identity (environment variables)

The harness exports these to every session — read them instead of guessing:

| Variable | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT` | workspace root (use for `--root`-free CLI calls) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL` | absolute path to this `SKILL.md` (never resolve it relative to the shell cwd) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_RUN` | run id (e.g. `0163`) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION` | this session's name (e.g. `0002-horizon-T-1`) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION_DIR` | this session's directory (transcript, usage.json, report) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` / `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS` | which round this is (0-based) / the run's planned total |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK` / `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK_TITLE` | the task id / title (full body: `"$HORIZON_BIN" task show "$ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK" --json`) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_PROJECTS` | comma-separated projects this task spans |
| `HORIZON_BIN`, `HORIZON_GIT` | absolute paths to the CLI and the ledger-git wrapper |
| `HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR`, `HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE` | the workspace ledger repo + its work tree — `"$HORIZON_GIT" …` is shorthand for `git --git-dir "$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree "$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" …` |

## Pace yourself (usage & interruption risk)

Sessions end for reasons you don't control: rate limits, usage caps, budgets.
The defense is NOT to avoid work — it is to make interruption cheap:

- **Commit at every coherent point** (plain git into the ledger, below). If
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` shows low budget headroom or recent
  `rate_limit`/`usage_limit` signals, commit what you have NOW and prefer
  finishing the piece in flight over opening a new front.
- If this is the run's **last round** (`ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` + 1 ==
  `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS`), leave the workspace hand-off-clean: commit, update
  the roadmap/task status, and write the report as if nobody continues today.
- Interrupted anyway? Nothing is lost that was committed — the next session
  resumes from the ledger (see "Resuming" below).

## One-shot discipline (important)

This session runs to completion and is **not resumed** — you will not be re-invoked
when a background job finishes. So **run work in the foreground and block on it**
(builds, checks, subagents). Anything you leave running in the background, or leave
uncommitted, may be lost when the session ends. Commit early and often (below).

## Pick the highest-value work

Read the roadmap and the live Lean state, then commit to the most valuable next
piece. A node being large, multi-session, or blocked on missing mathlib
infrastructure is **not** a reason to skip it — start it, build the missing
lemma/definition yourself as project-local infrastructure, and push it as far as
you genuinely can. Prefer ambitious progress over defensive avoidance.

If this session was launched on a specific task, make concrete progress on that
task's REAL objective — don't preemptively pivot to easy unrelated wins because
the objective is large. Leave a concise task comment only for a durable state
change or blocker, not every action. You own the task's terminal status (skill:
`task-status`): set `--status done` only when the objective is FULLY complete;
`blocked`/`failed` if genuinely stuck; set nothing if it's only partly advanced
(it returns to the queue).

## Fresh-context checkpoints

The old Ground pass is no longer a second orchestrator role, but independent
review is still part of convergence. Spawn the **`ground`** subagent at these
checkpoints:

- before marking a multi-step task `done`;
- after every two substantive Horizon sessions on a long-running task;
- immediately after a strategy pivot, a broad workspace edit, or a surprising
  clean/build result.

Give it the task/project scope and ask it to inspect the actual ledger diff,
blueprint graph, Lean state, roadmap, inbox, and reports with fresh context. It
is read-only on source and reports issues/memory; reconcile its findings before
continuing. Use **`work-reviewer`** for a narrow diff/proof audit and **`janitor`**
when the main concern is workspace hygiene. A one-session task may skip the
periodic checkpoint, but must still obtain a fresh-context review before a
terminal `done` claim.

Schedule upkeep even when the last command did not print a warning. On a
multi-session run, dispatch **`janitor` at the start of every second Horizon
session** and before the final report; on a one-session task, dispatch it once
before claiming completion if the run touched roadmap, task, or inbox state.
Record the checkpoint in the report and wait for the helper before continuing.
If `janitor` is unavailable, ask **`ground`** for the same hygiene inspection;
Ground is read-only, so apply or explicitly record its findings yourself.

## Warnings are work

Commands report problems for a reason — never scroll past them. `lake build`
warnings, `horizon graph sync` warnings, roadmap consistency warnings, deprecation
notices from any tool: if your change caused it, **fix it now** (it is part of
the task); if it's pre-existing or caused by the tool/command itself, don't
silently ignore it — record it as a memory item, file an inbox `issue`, or
address it `--to human` when a human decision is needed. A warning that
survives your session should be one you *chose* to leave, with a trace saying
why.

Collection-health warnings are a dispatch trigger, not background noise. When
`inbox`, `roadmap`, or `task` reports an overloaded queue, stale running item,
or status mismatch, pause the proof loop and spawn **`janitor`** with the
workspace scope. Wait for it, reconcile its report, rerun the command, and
record any warning that remains intentionally. Do this at most once for the
same warning in a session; a persistent warning still needs a report or inbox
issue rather than repeated no-op calls.

## Do the work (Lean)

For any Lean edit, load `lean-check` before touching the file and follow its
required LSP loop: query the target with `lean_diagnostic_messages` or
`lean_goal` before the first edit and after each subsequent edit. Keep `lake
build` for the final session boundary or a specifically required kernel check;
LSP is enough between edits and proof obligations. Use the narrowest `lake env
lean` fallback when LSP is unavailable, and do not duplicate that check when the
configured final build covers the same files.

**Do not `grep` for a lemma.** Grep matches names you already guessed; it cannot
find the lemma whose name you don't know, and that is the one that costs you an
afternoon. This workspace indexes every declaration in every project *and* in
mathlib — query it:

| You want | Use | Not |
|---|---|---|
| "does this lemma exist, anywhere?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" search "<words or name>" --json` | `grep -r` |
| "what's the lemma for this *statement*?" | LSP `lean_leansearch` (natural language) | guessing names |
| "what matches this *type*?" | LSP `lean_loogle` (`Nat → ?a → ?a`) | `grep` |
| "does something in scope close this goal?" | LSP `lean_local_search` / `lean_hover_info` | reading files |
| "what should I prove next?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` (ranked) | scanning the blueprint |
| "what does this node depend on / block?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> get label:<id>` | reading imports |
| "is the proof right?" | `lake env lean <file>` (narrowest faithful check) | `lean_diagnostic_messages` alone |

`"$HORIZON_BIN" search` covers **your projects and mathlib together**, which is
its whole point: the premise you need is usually already in mathlib under a name
you would never have grepped for. One query costs a second; re-proving an
existing lemma costs a session. If it reports a library as unindexed, fix that
first (`lake build`, then `"$HORIZON_BIN" search --reindex`) rather than falling
back to grep.

Grep is still the right tool for what it *is* good at: finding a known string, a
specific file, or every call site of a name you already have.

- Search before proving — the lemma may already exist. Skill: `leansearch`.
- Use the **Lean LSP MCP** for tight proof feedback, then verify with the narrowest
  faithful `lake` / `lake env lean` check. Skill: `lean-check`.
- Use the DAG to choose and scope work, not just to report it. Skill: `hgraph`.
- When editing blueprint material, follow the house format. Skill: `blueprint-conventions`.
  The blueprint is timeless mathematics, never a formalization journal. Put Lean
  implementation notes, failed tactics, and declaration-specific progress on the
  corresponding hgraph node with `graph add comment`; do not insert
  "Formalization note" paragraphs into blueprint `.tex` files.

## Read the other projects

They are in this workspace for a reason: the same lemma, pattern, or dead end has
often already been worked out next door. `"$HORIZON_BIN" search` spans **all**
projects — an existing construction in another project is a lead, whether you
import it, copy the approach, or read its blueprint. `references/` holds the
original sources (skill: `references`). Staying inside your own project because
the task named it is how the workspace re-derives the same thing three times.

## Delegating beyond your team (ask permission first)

Your normal way to parallelize is **within** your team: spawn subagents/workers
(skill: `subagents`) and dispatch scoped work to them in the foreground. That
needs no permission.

      "body": "[persistent] HUMAN DECISION, BINDING (2026-07-28): DivFamZar is widened to ARBITRARY AFFINE OPEN pieces. R2 of I-0346 is chosen and closed; R1 (the GL_2/Aut(P1) route) is NOT to be built.\n\nTHE RULE, for any session on the DD-R certificate lane or its consumers:\n\n 1. DO NOT BUILD THE GL_2(k) ACTION ON P1. Roadmap leaf AJCR.w4-rep.datum.dat-d.ddr.certificate.p1-aut stays pending and DEPRIORITISED \u2014 not rejected (R1 may still accelerate the large-field case one day), but no session spends time on it, and no consumer may be written against it. Same for any descent work whose only purpose is to rescue R1.\n\n 2. The widening target: FinCoverData s pieces become arbitrary affine opens rather than basic opens of a FIXED PAIR of pinned P1 charts. Justification to use, not to re-derive: supp D is finite over R, hence lies in a single affine open of C x_k Spec R (Stacks 0B8B); spec-dd-r.md ADDENDUM 4 carries the argument.\n\n 3. THE CHART-WISE PARTITIONS OF UNITY ARE WHAT HAS TO GO. Per-piece swallow-or-miss needs only openness (DivSchemeCertZarConn.lean uses only openness); it is the partitions that upgrade inside one piece to inside one chart. Removing them will break consumers \u2014 repair the consumers deliberately, and do not smuggle the old typing back in by typing pieces INTO the charts (DivisorFamily.lean h0/h1/pieces is exactly the pattern that made the previous cheaper option vacuous).\n\n 4. TWO OBLIGATIONS THE WIDENING RELOCATES RATHER THAN REMOVES, both to be discharged explicitly and neither to be hidden inside a LocalEquations: (i) fibrewise-finite support, which must come from the seed s own degree data; (ii) whatever the old fixed-pair confinement was silently supplying to the certificate clauses.\n\n 5. THE STANDING NEGATIVE RESULTS REMAIN BINDING, all established by predecessor sessions and adversarially checked. Chart-avoid is NO. The counterexample is FIELD-INDEPENDENT, so enlarging the field is not an escape. And the sharp form to quote: NO repair that keeps the pieces inside the preimages of a FIXED PAIR of points of P1 can work. The joint-cover variant is refuted (leaf ...joint-cover, rejected) \u2014 do not retry it.\n\nWHY R2 AND NOT A FIELD-SIZE HYPOTHESIS: archon-protected.yaml freezes the arbitrary-field statement, so |P1(k)| >= n+2 would answer a different question. R2 is the only field-uniform fix. The sharpness result (leaf ...field-size, done) stands and needs no further human input.\n\nFull reasoning: I-0346 (human comment, 2026-07-28).       "body": "[persistent] [persistent] REPRESENTABILITY PUSH, 2026-07-29 \u2014 the claim/lane protocol that makes 10 free-objective lanes not collide.\n\nWHY THIS EXISTS. This round replaces prescriptive per-leaf tasks with FIVE lanes per project: one REVIEWER and four PROVERS ranked p1..p4. The provers each pick their own target. That only works if claiming is explicit and public. This item is the claiming mechanism. Read it before your first edit.\n\nTHE FIVE LANES PER PROJECT\n- `review-ajc` / `review-ajcr` \u2014 reviewer. Read-mostly. Finds defects of ROUTE and ORGANISATION, not of individual proofs; may propose refactors and file tasks-as-proposals for the provers. Does not race provers for proof work.\n- `ajc-p1` / `ajcr-p1` \u2014 takes the MOST important open representability item.\n- `-p2`, `-p3`, `-p4` \u2014 2nd, 3rd, 4th most important, where \"important\" is measured against the project's representability headline, not by ease.\n\nCLAIMING \u2014 do this BEFORE you start proving, not after.\n 1. `horizon roadmap list --focus <your project's w4-rep / picrep subtree>` and read the reviewer's open notes.\n 2. Pick your item. Check no other lane owns it: an item with `--owner` set to another lane IS CLAIMED. Do not take it, even if you think you would be faster.\n 3. Claim it: `horizon roadmap set <id> --owner <your-task-id> --status active`. If your target is not yet a roadmap item, `roadmap add` it under the right parent first, then claim it.\n 4. Announce: one `horizon inbox add --kind info --to horizon --body \"CLAIM <lane>: <roadmap id> \u2014 <one line on what discharging it buys>\"`.\n 5. Release on exit: if you did NOT finish, `roadmap set <id> --owner ''` and leave a one-line inbox note saying where you stopped and what the next lane should NOT re-derive. An item left owned by a dead lane is worse than an unclaimed one.\n\nRANK IS A TIE-BREAK, NOT A FENCE. If p1's item turns out to be blocked on p3's, say so in the inbox and swap \u2014 rank exists so four lanes do not all converge on the same top item, not to stop you working on the right thing. p1 has first refusal on any contested item.\n\nYOU MAY PROPOSE WORK TO THE OTHER LANES. Direct-message with `horizon inbox add --kind hint --to task:<lane-id> --body \"\u2026\"`. A good proposal names the declaration, the file, and why it is worth more than what that lane currently holds. You may NOT reassign another lane's claimed item, and you may NOT create new horizon runs or tasks for teams outside your own (`horizon permissions` is false on both counts \u2014 propose to the human instead).\n\nSTANDING BINDING DECISIONS you must not relitigate: `I-0491` (AJC: no rational-point binder on the headline; `hasRationalPoint_of_curve` is FALSE and must be deleted, never proved) and `I-0492` (AJCR: `DivFamZar` widens to arbitrary affine opens; do NOT build the GL_2/Aut(P1) route). Read both.\n\nWHAT COUNTS AS PROGRESS, given the 2026-07-29 audit. That audit found 99 of 101 sampled representability claims refuted: 67 sorry-reachable, 17 VACUOUS, 12 hypothesis-shifted. So the bar is explicit:\n- A discharged obligation must be sorry-free AND its hypotheses must be inhabitable. Before you claim a gate closed, exhibit a witness for every antecedent, or say plainly which antecedent is still undischarged.\n- Do NOT add a class, structure field, or hypothesis whose statement does not mention the object it is supposedly about. `HasDivFunctor` is the cautionary case: its field asserted only that a presheaf category is nonempty, `C` did not occur, and it was advertised as the existence of the relative divisor functor. That is a vacuity, and it survived because nobody read the statement.\n- Do NOT discharge an obligation by projecting the hypothesis you assumed (`choose_spec.1` of your own binder). That is `P \u2192 P`.\n- A green `lake build` is not evidence a statement is non-vacuous. Check imports are current before believing a `lean_multi_attempt` success.\n\nCOMMIT DISCIPLINE. This is ONE shared ledger branch with 10 writers. Another lane's integrate sweep can commit your half-written file before you have measured it once.
